source.snippet: "You know what does work? Adblock. It reasons that we could build a new form of it. I would pay for som[ething like this]" — HN commenter on 'Advertise in ChatGPT' thread, July 2026. Commenter references open-weights models (Kimi) and distillation to CPU as the enabling technology for a new generation of AI-powered ad/content filtering.

problem_statement: As AI assistants (ChatGPT, Gemini, etc.) begin serving sponsored content and ads, users have no tool to detect, label, or filter AI-generated advertising responses — the same problem Adblock solved for the web, now emerging for LLM interfaces.
target_segment: Privacy-conscious power users and developers who already pay for ad-blocking tools or VPNs, and who use AI assistants daily for work.
notes: Buyer intent present ('I would pay for') but problem is still nascent — ChatGPT ads are just rolling out. Early-mover window exists. Adblock/uBlock have proven willingness-to-pay (donations, premium tiers) in this demographic. Signal is speculative but timely given the July 2026 context of ChatGPT advertising launch.
